newsitem.title: UK: Zinc rally lures LME options players into market.
newsitem.headline: Zinc rally lures LME options players into market.

text.p: A rally in zinc futures sparked fresh interest in LME options on Thursday, boosting volatilities slightly, but turnover was spotty.
Some of the business in zinc and copper was from producers eager to lock in high prices, some traders said.

The main focus on Thursday morning was on July $1,350 puts and $1,400 calls. The $1,350s traded as high as high as 22.25 percent implied volatility, compared to Wednesday's evening evaluation of 22.60 percent.
LME three months shot up to a fresh 4-3/4 year peak of $1,389 per tonne in Thursday morning activity.
Some traders said producers were active in zinc, but others were unsure of the source of the business.
One trader said Far Eastern producers were buying nearby puts and selling forward calls, such as fourth quarter $1,450s.
"Market makers were short upside calls so they were happy to buy them," he added.
Implied at-the-money (ATM) volatility was quoted for July at 21.0/23.0 percent, August at 20.5/22 percent and September at 20.0/21.5 percent.
Copper also saw producer activity in a wide range of dates, from nearbys to far forwards.
One trader saw $2,650 puts done for July at 23.50 percent volatility and another said first quarter 1998 downsides were also in demand.
LME data showed July-March 1998 $2,100 strikes traded at $30.00 on Thursday morning.
"You can't blame the producers. These are quite good numbers for them," a trader said.
Still another player said producer business in Asian put options had been done for the year 2000 at 85-90 cents/lb ($1,874-$1,984/tonne).
In other activity, trade had been seen on Wednesday in August $2,700 calls at around 21 percent.
ATM volatility, however, was little changed.
July was quoted at 22.0/24.0 percent, August at 20.0/21.5 percent and December at 16.5/17.5 percent. The first half of 1998 was around 16.0 percent, with a premium of one point for downsides.
In the aluminium sector, rumours went through the market on Wednesday that enquiries had been made for a big lump -- said to be around 1,000 lots -- of average 1998 $1,800 calls.
Several dealers said they doubted any business had been done. One suggested it may be a U.S. consumer who last week bought 1999 options.
Volatility edged up on the talk of call buying, but slipped back on Thursday morning. July was quoted at 15.5/17.5 percent, August at 16.0/17.25 percent and average 1998 at 15.0/15.75 percent.
Tuesday's sell off in three month futures to $1,565 also saw put granting from directional players, one dealer said.
Another said August strangles at $1,550/$1,625 were done at valuation.
LME data showed 1,100 lots of August $1,550 TAPOS were traded on Monday, pushing up open interest by 500 lots.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
